newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Petrobras eyes 68 firms for partnerships.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras eyes 68 firms for partnerships.

text.p: Brazilian state oil monopoly Petrobras said it drafted a list of 68 firms, including oil giants from the United States and Europe, for a possible future joint ventures on oil and gas projects.

A Petrobras spokeswoman said the list includes U.S. behemoths Texaco Inc, Exxon Corp and Chevron and Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Royal Dutch Shell. Petrobras had offered the market some 138 exploration and production projects, including the large Albacora Leste oil and natural gas field in Rio de Janeiro state, she said.
The list was made up of companies that expressed an interest in signing agreements with Petrobras to gain access to geological and geophysical data on projects offered by the state firm, she added.

The spokeswoman said Petrobras hopes to sign the joint- venture accords in July and attract nearly a billion reais ($950 million) in exploration investment from partnerships. The figure could reach 3.5 billion reais in development and production.

The joint ventures will be possible only after Congress approves Brazil's new Oil Law, which will end Petrobras' monopoly. The law would give Petrobras three months to announce which areas it intends to continue developing and a new National Oil Agency will grant concessions based on the state firm's capacity to finance the projects, officials said.
